scenario.title: Deciding and setting up database governance
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
scenario.review: Older research may describe heavier onboarding. Apply minimum activation and optional-adoption boundaries first.
questions: Decide the first-use explanation of adopting Yoke Python migration modules versus retaining an existing migration owner; no universal migration adapter was demonstrated.

lessons.title: Offer governance in plain terms
lessons.when: Onboard execution profile surveys migrations or user starts database-changing work
lessons.need: Explain what Yoke governs before choosing: declare now, attach later, no Yoke-governed database, or undecided. External ownership/no DB/unsupported kind is a complete no-governance answer; undecided blocks profile confirmation today.
lessons.surface: Onboard profile governed-database box and governed-database branches.
lessons.gap: The current offer is buried in the upfront profile. JOURNEYS plans later timing but has no explicit first-database-change offer. Proposed cue should appear then and retain the recorded choice.
recipes: yoke projects capability-settings get --project P --cap-type migration_model --json

lessons.title: Disclose the supported models first
lessons.when: Before agreeing to governance for an existing database
lessons.need: Current validator supports SQLite/local validation and Postgres/external validation, both with Python governed migration modules. MySQL and external-adapter runners are explicitly unsupported. Postgres requires stack/database/output coordinates, not just any connection string.
lessons.surface: Migration model pairing matrix and capability validator.
lessons.gap: Surface these limits before collecting credentials or implying Alembic/Prisma/other migration frameworks can be adopted unchanged. Unsupported is not incomplete install.

lessons.title: Gather and verify project-owned facts
lessons.when: User chooses a supported model now
lessons.need: Read exact authoritative location, separate validation target/provisioning, migration directory, connection variable and membership/digest/serving-floor ledger. Write the complete capability through the registered surface and read back. Onboarding neither applies nor rehearses migrations.
lessons.surface: governed-database lines 25–34 and 57–68; deep capability contract.
lessons.gap: Postgres declaration is taught through a reference still heavy with Yoke source-dev examples; add a complete external-project route without copying Yoke defaults or exposing control-plane credentials.
recipes: yoke projects capability-settings get --project P --cap-type migration_model --json

lessons.title: Defer without pretending readiness
lessons.when: Known model lacks stack/coordinates or user keeps external schema ownership
lessons.need: Record known facts and missing coordinates for attach-later; do not write a placeholder capability. No-governance keeps item DB claims at none. A failed write stops with the exact validator requirement.
lessons.surface: governed-database attach-later, no-governance and failure branches.
lessons.gap: Future timing must reopen a deferred choice when the missing facts exist, while respecting a settled no-governance answer.
